leftEvidence.title: The sacrifice is eaten in one house during the departure setting

points.label: Place
points.left: One house governs the meat within the first ordinance.
points.right: A chosen central place governs sacrifice and eating in the land.

points.label: Morning
points.left: Nothing is carried outside and the departure occurs that day.
points.right: The worshiper returns to tents in the morning.

points.label: Memory
points.left: The rule closes with the LORD bringing Israel from Egypt.
points.right: The rule repeatedly names the night departure and lifelong memory.

payload.posture: Keep each Scripture witness intact, inspect what each states, and do not supply a combined sequence the sources do not author.

rightEvidence.title: The sacrifice is offered and eaten where the LORD chooses

payload.tension: The two laws locate the observance differently while each anchors it in departure from Egypt.
payload.title: One house and the chosen place
